D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling “off” for maybe…seven months? It’s hard to pin down. I mostly just feel flat. Things that used to matter at the library—new grants, circulation numbers, even the board praising a project—barely register. I go through the motions, but it’s like I’m on autopilot.

Sleep doesn’t help. I’m in bed enough hours, but I wake up exhausted, like I haven’t rested at all. I find myself pacing the aisles before we open, straightening the same shelf over and over, rubbing my hands or picking at my cuticles without realizing it. I can’t seem to sit still in my own office.

Around six months ago, I started getting these fixed ideas about a colleague I’m close to. We’re not officially together, but I’m convinced she’s seeing someone else behind my back. There’s no real proof, but I can’t shake it. I’ve even thought the “other person” is hiding in the stacks.

Sometimes, especially when I’m closing up, I see figures between the shelves or in my peripheral vision—a man standing by the reference desk, a child darting past—but when I look directly, no one’s there. When people ask what’s wrong, I start to answer and end up talking about some old cataloging system or a completely different topic.

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h001.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve just felt really low for… maybe seven months now? Hard to be exact. It started as just feeling down, but over time it’s like someone turned the dimmer switch on my whole life. I move slower, even pushing the mop or bending to pick up trash feels like it’s in slow motion. My wife says I shuffle around the apartment like an old man, and I don’t really want to see the grandkids or talk to anyone at work on my breaks anymore. I mostly sit by myself in the supply closet.

Nights are rough. I lie there for hours, staring at the ceiling, not able to fall asleep. My mind keeps going to this idea that everything’s winding down, like the building, the city, maybe the whole world is about to just stop. It doesn’t feel like a worry, more like a fact I can’t shake.

Sometimes I feel things crawling or brushing on my skin, like tiny bugs on my arms or back, but there’s nothing there. And I catch myself using… I call them “dustwords,” little words that only make sense to me, and people look at me funny when I say them. My work’s slipping; I miss spots, forget keys, and it all just feels heavier than it used to.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h002.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h011.question:

I know the guys think I’m weird—sometimes I’ll stop mid-task and do things in a very specific way, like tapping the wrench three times or turning my head a certain way before I move. I can’t explain it; it just feels like I have to.  

I hear voices a lot, especially when it’s noisy on deck or at night in the bunk. They call my name, or say things like “you did this” or “it’s your fault,” but no one’s there. I used to hang out with the crew, play cards, video chat with people on shore. Now I mostly stay in my cabin.  

I don’t really enjoy anything anymore—food, movies, talking to anyone. I’m constantly pacing the corridor or picking at my arms, like I can’t settle. I keep thinking I’ve messed everything up—my job, my family, even the accidents on the platform, like somehow I caused them just by being here.  

Sometimes I think it’d be easier if I just wasn’t around at all. I catch myself going over ways I could disappear, even though I haven’t actually done anything. It’s gotten harder to concentrate on instructions, and sometimes when I talk, the words just… fall apart and people stare at me like they don’t understand what I’m saying.
